And, I mean, the Serbs, the Serbs in Zvornik itself were in jeopardy and the Muslims who had returned. So practically one could not go on living with them and we saw -- I don't know if I'm right. It was at the end of June I think, we thought that we were being saved by the legal police, when they came from Pale, Mr. Karisik. And in two or three hours they arrested them in different buildings, they took them away, they convicted them, and then we breathed a sigh of relief. And now, what the relations were among them, I mean, do you understand this? The authorities had to do what they had to do. They couldn't get rid of them in any other way but the way that I've just described to you now, as it ultimately happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, let's look at some documents which illustrate the relationship that the authorities had with the paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Could we please see P2867.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zelenovic, this is Zvornik interim government decision dated the 27th of April, 1992, and it's signed by Mr. Grujic as president of the interim government. And it states in Article 1 that: "Permission is hereby given to purchase material for the manufacturing of uniforms for the Igor Markovic special unit of the TO." Now, as I've told you, the Trial Chamber is aware that the Igor Markovic special unit is another name for the Yellow Wasps. So this document shows Grujic providing the Yellow Wasps with logistical support. So it's not a case of the authorities not standing up to the Yellow Wasps; rather, it's a case of them actively assisting them, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR ZELENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Madam Prosecutor, it can also be put this way, that these things, that is to say, knowing Grujic very well, and as far as I can remember it's been a long time, he was even beaten up by these same people. So their hand was forced as far as the paramilitaries are concerned, and I know that personally because we're friends, you know. I know his personal opinion about the paramilitaries, all these paramilitary formations. So this decision was forced. It can be interpreted in this way rather than what you had said. That is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Mr. Zelenovic, there is an abundance of evidence on the record of Mr. Grujic and the government providing logistical assistance, payment of salaries to not just Arkan's unit, not just the Yellow Wasps, but the White Eagles, the Aleksic's group, Niski's group and Pivarski's group who were all on the payroll of the Zvornik TO. Now, I'd just like to show you P2913. So it's your evidence that Mr. Grujic was forced into providing this assistance to the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR ZELENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, all these documents -- I mean, well, he had to cover this in financial terms, but this is how it arrived. I mean, on the basis of what I talked about then and when I asked them for help and -- what do I call them, these paramilitary -- these paramilitaries threatened the factory. And he said nothing, you can do nothing, you can just be a victim, like me -- I mean, I'm talking on behalf of Grujic now. And he had to cover himself in material terms. That is how I see this, because I heard this from him with my very own ears. That is the only way I see this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Well, let's look at a document that he wrote at the time which is on the screen in front of you, which is a request dated the 6th of June, 1992, from the Zvornik interim government and it's signed by Mr. Grujic. And it's stamped the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the same date. And he is informing the republican authorities that TO members from the territory of the municipality received payments for April 1992 in a total amount of 32.100.000 dinars. And he's asking to effect the payment for the arming of the police members for the month of May. Now, this is a document, Mr. Zelenovic, that specifically discusses payments to the TO in April and May. We've just discussed the fact that the paramilitaries were paid as members of the TO during that period, and yet in this document to the republican authorities there is no mention of the fact that the payments were coerced in any way. In fact, Mr. Grujic just requests more funding. So surely if Mr. Grujic was being forced into paying the paramilitaries as part of the TO, he would have mentioned this to the republican authorities in his letter on exactly that topic?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR ZELENOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look, if you're done with your question, it was hard. These were very hard times, and to try to deal with these people, I mean directly and these clashes, you risked your head. And to put anything on paper from that point of view, as you had put it, that would have been a stupid thing to do. I tell you, I fled from the factory because they left and somebody said there, "Hey, he tricked you into taking an engine that wasn't working." I wasn't even at the factory, I was in Serbia. You see, that's how I see it. Who was not in that situation cannot -- I mean, well, you can put whatever, hundreds of these sort of, what, evidence, things here. But I've given you my opinion about this. 100 per cent, I stand behind this 100 per cent. Grujic cannot say and write to I don't know who, Radovan Karadzic, and say, "You know what? I'm under threat by these and those." They were in all pores. Quite simply, nothing could function. Believe me. After the 29th of June I think, I mean when they were arrested, that is to say -- well, you could not even be in peace in your own apartment, nowhere, so that was really a sigh of relief. For us it was as if it was an occupation force that was strangling us every day and we were just waiting. It was unbearable. Their main task was to walk around, to loot shops. I don't know. I mean, let me not qualify them. It was impossible for the authorities to do anything. They were powerless. They were a lot more powerful. They were armed. People with troubled backgrounds. So that was it. The authorities had to behave the way they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zelenovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does it mean you have more?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCKENNA
utterances.text: I do have perhaps ten minutes more if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue tomorrow then. Mr. Zelenovic, we'll adjourn for today and continue tomorrow. I'd like to advise you not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony while you are giving evidence. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of June, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.
